title: Model Shift Guardian: Console dashboard and incident channels for quality drift
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Create a Console-first experience that surfaces quality drift associated with model and configuration changes and routes consolidated, deduplicated notifications into customer channels (Slack + PagerDuty). The feature will bind eval results to change events, provide a compact incident summary, and reduce noisy paging by grouping similar regressions using deterministic fingerprints and temporal suppression.
acceptance_criteria: Console dashboard shows a timeline view with change events (model version, config_hash, rollout_id) and correlated eval score deltas for at least 3 curated eval suites
Notifications sent to Slack channels and PagerDuty services contain a grouped summary (fingerprint id, top 3 affected metrics, link to diff view) rather than one message per failing eval
Dedupe algorithm groups related signals for a configurable window (default 30 minutes) and suppresses duplicates to PagerDuty unless cardinality exceeds threshold
Telemetry: per-change false positive rate and time-to-notify tracked in the observability pipeline, dashboarded under console-telemetry
End-to-end tests validate non-regression: a simulated model roll upgrade that triggers metric drop of >5% surfaces a single PD incident and a single Slack thread with actionable links
notes: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with Reliability, Runtime, and Console teams. Alignment on binding eval_id to change events produced by the changefeed service.
2026-03-02: Design review — product + design agreed on compact card layout with inline diff, ability to expand to full eval trace. Action: design to provide mocks for mobile and narrow consoles.
2026-03-05: Eng spike completed — prototype fingerprint generation (sha256 of model_version + config_hash + eval_suite identifier) demonstrates stable grouping across replayed events.
2026-03-09: Security requested review of PagerDuty integration flow and service account scoping. Security review flagged PD escalation keys must be rotated monthly.
2026-03-12: PM pulled in two enterprise beta customers for early feedback on dedupe thresholds and PD routing policies. Initial feedback prefers sticky grouping per rollout for first 24h.
2026-03-13: Merged API contract PR that exposes change_event_id on eval results and a summarized diff endpoint (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4289).
decisions: Use deterministic fingerprint: H = sha256(model_version || config_hash || eval_suite || metric_window_start) to group signals. This avoids expensive similarity clustering in the hot path.
Default dedupe TTL will be 30 minutes for PagerDuty, 2 hours for Slack threads. Both configurable per-customer via Console policy.
PagerDuty receives only high-cardinality or high-severity grouped incidents; lower-severity groups go to Slack only with an option to escalate.
Console will surface a single canonical 'change incident' with links to the involved evals, raw diffs, and runbook suggestions from the Knowledge Base.

Need finalized eval-suite canonical naming from Applied ML — pending (PM-90234)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Feature flag enabled for internal org only. Validate grouping heuristics and PD behavior with simulated traffic.
Phase 1 (beta): Enable for 3 enterprise customers with option to tweak dedupe windows and severity thresholds.
Phase 2 (GA): Default on for all orgs, admin controls exposed in Console settings. Provide migration notes for customers using legacy eval webhooks.
Rollback: Console hides PD routing and reverts to per-eval notifications if dedupe service reports >5% misgrouping rate over 1h window.
metrics: Time-to-notify (median) from change_event -> first Slack message
PagerDuty noise ratio: number of PD incidents per unique change_event
Grouping accuracy: percent of eval signals correctly grouped under a single fingerprint (benchmarked with labelled replay dataset)
Customer escalation rate: fraction of grouped incidents that the customer escalates to S1 within 24h
